summary: Round 3, scoped to the delta since 006aa9aad9dd. The two mechanical changes are sound and measured: the field rename `keys` -> `logKeys` is complete (four references in CommitLog, no other reference in the tree, private field so no test touches it) and changes no behaviour; the new fourth LogKeysTest case genuinely pins both length guards -- I deleted each guard in my own tree and got `java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at LogKeysTest.java:80` for the startsWith deletion and a failure for the endsWith deletion, so the backlog row's claim about `begin > end` is true as stated. I also re-measured the paragraph's own falsifiable claim: swapping `new CommitLog(store, prefix, chainEpoch).keyFor(0)` for `new LogKeys(prefix, chainEpoch).keyFor(0)` in firstEntry leaves :sequencer:test green, so 'the throw is unreachable from here' is correct. Nothing in this delta touches an object-store request; the request rate is unchanged and still scales with segments, not with keys under the prefix. The prose, however, has fixed one measured-false claim and introduced two more, which is the pattern this file keeps hitting: the rewritten ChainReplay paragraph misattributes the M4.23 warning to `neverOpened` (which names M4.6d and M5) and asserts M4.23 loosens the `chainEpoch >= 1` test (it does not); and the new test's comment calls a short key under the prefix unreachable until M4.8b2, when a LIST can return one today and M4.8b2's own row gives no support for its writer asking this question at all. Both are minor and land under `minors-land`; I would delete the unverifiable clauses rather than redraft them a fourth time. Process note, not a finding: this is round 3 against `two-round-cap` and `baselines/review.txt` carries no staged `rounds:M4.8b1` argument, so check-reviewed.sh will refuse the commit until one is added.

findings.title: The rewritten ChainReplay paragraph replaces one measured-false claim with two more: `neverOpened` does not name M4.23, and M4.23 does not loosen the `chainEpoch >= 1` test
findings.detail: The new second paragraph ends: '{@link #neverOpened} already names M4.23 as the change that loosens exactly that test. Anyone doing it must add the check here.' Two clauses, both false. (1) `neverOpened`'s javadoc (ChainReplay.java lines 231-263) names M4.6d's rerouting and M5's forwarding as the candidates; it never mentions M4.23. The only other M4.23 mention in the file is in `firstInheritableAncestor`'s javadoc at line 314. `grep -n 'M4\.23' sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/ChainReplay.java` returns exactly lines 48 and 314. (2) What `firstInheritableAncestor` actually attributes to M4.23 is the origin caveat -- a wholly empty `prevEpoch` is not walked past -- and M4.23's own row (docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md line 185) is about `checkLink` in Invariants, the depth cap, and `neverOpened`'s `sealed.sequence() == 0` precision. None of that touches `chainEpoch >= 1`. Closing M4.23's gap makes the walk-back run FURTHER (more `chainEpoch--` iterations, so the guard is exercised more), it does not loosen the guard. Failure scenario, and it is the same one the round-2 finding named one draft earlier: whoever picks up M4.23 is sent to `neverOpened` for a warning that is not there, finds a different warning about M4.6d/M5 instead, and reads that the paragraph applies only to someone loosening `>= 1` -- which they are not doing. So the warning does not fire on the change that actually moves `neverOpened`'s semantics, which is precisely the change it was written for. The same two errors are now also in the authoritative task list (docs/internal/product/backlog-done.md line 107: '`neverOpened` already names M4.23 as the change that LOOSENS exactly that loop condition'). Secondary imprecision in the same paragraph: 'Both callers test {@code chainEpoch >= 1} in the same short-circuited expression' is true only of `firstInheritableAncestor` (line 326, `while (chainEpoch >= 1 && neverOpened(firstEntry(...)))`); in `replayAncestry` the guard is the loop condition at line 173 and the call is in the body at line 174, which is guarded but not short-circuited. And 'a {@code Continue} whose {@code prevEpoch} is bounded only from above' is bounded from below too -- `Continue`'s compact constructor throws on `prevEpoch < 0` and the field decodes from a uvarint -- so the only non-positive epoch any of the three routes can reach is exactly 0, which `CommitLog`'s constructor accepts (it throws only on `epoch < 0`). The accurate minimal repair is to name `firstInheritableAncestor` rather than `neverOpened` and to say M4.23 makes this walk go further back rather than that it loosens the test; the better one, given three rounds of this paragraph, is to delete the forward-looking clauses and keep only the two sentences that are measured -- leftover, not guard, and the swap is green.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M4.23 follows this paragraph to neverOpened for the warning it says is there, finds instead a warning about M4.6d and M5, and reads that the paragraph applies only to someone loosening `chainEpoch >= 1` -- which M4.23 does not do. The warning therefore does not fire on the change it was written for: closing M4.23's empty-prevEpoch gap makes firstInheritableAncestor's walk-back run further, past epochs it does not today, with the only thing standing between it and a CommitLog constructed at a non-positive epoch being a loop condition the paragraph has just told the author is somebody else's problem.

findings.title: The new test's comment calls a short key unreachable until M4.8b2; a LIST can return one today, and M4.8b2's row does not say its writer asks this question
findings.detail: The comment on `aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing` says the case is 'UNREACHABLE FROM TODAY'S TWO CALL SITES, which only ever pass keys that came back from `store.list(logPrefix, ...)`. It stops being unreachable in M4.8b2, whose writer asks this question about a key it is ABOUT to write rather than one it listed.' Coming back from a LIST does not make a key long enough. `BinStore.list(logPrefix, ...)` returns every object under the prefix, and this task exists precisely because foreign objects appear there -- a foreign object named `<logPrefix>x` is exactly the second assertion in this test and is returned by the same LIST that `ChainReplay.applyChain` (line 338) and `ChainReplay.chainEnd` (line 116) already run against production data. So the endsWith guard is load-bearing on today's paths, not on a future one; the comment understates the hazard rather than overstating it. The M4.8b2 half is unsupported: M4.8b2's row (docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md line 333) specifies a writer that PUTs at `ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch:016x>/ckpt/<seq:016x>.ckpt` and says nothing about calling `isEntryKey` on anything, so 'its writer asks this question about a key it is ABOUT to write' is a prediction about a task that has not been designed, offered as the justification for the test. Failure scenario: a later reader takes the comment at its word, concludes the two guards and this test are speculative pre-work for M4.8b2, and if M4.8b2 lands in a different shape deletes them -- reintroducing an unchecked StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on a recovery path that genuinely reaches short foreign keys, which is the failure mode this task exists to remove. The test itself is correct and both guards are measured dead-on-deletion; only its stated reason needs to change from 'reachable in M4.8b2' to 'reachable from today's LIST'.
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader takes the comment at its word -- the short-key case is unreachable until M4.8b2 -- and, when M4.8b2 lands in a shape that never calls isEntryKey (its row specifies only a PUT at ckpt/<seq>.ckpt), deletes the two length guards and this test as speculative pre-work. A foreign object named `<logPrefix>x`, which store.list returns to applyChain and chainEnd on exactly the path this task exists to fix, then makes substring(begin > end) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException during recovery: LocalSequencer.start releases the lease, the next node repeats, and nothing deletes the object -- the permanent takeover loop M4.8b1 was written to remove, arriving through the door it just closed.
